sourceEnglishTitle: Training a New Crew Member on Nailing
sourceEnglishObjective: Coach a new roofer on nailing with clear commands, correcting mistakes without embarrassing them
sourceEnglishSpeaking: You are training the AI, a new crew member, on the nail gun: show where to nail, check their work, and correct mistakes with commands like clávalo aquí and no lo hundas, keeping the tone supportive.

sourceGrammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (clávalo aquí, no lo hundas)

examples.es: Clávalo aquí, en la zona de clavado.
examples.en: Nail it here, in the nailing zone.

examples.es: No lo hundas; déjalo al ras.
examples.en: Don't sink it; leave it flush.

example.target: Clávalo aquí, en la zona de clavado.
example.native: Nail it here, in the nailing zone.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Tú command with a pronoun: clávalo; negative: no lo claves.

example.native: Pull it out and put in another one.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Negative tú command: no lo saques (c changes to qu).
The negative tú command uses the subjunctive: no lo hundas.

example.native: Let me know and we'll adjust it together.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Affirmative command: ajústalo; the pronoun is attached to the end.
In a negative command the pronoun goes before the verb: no la apuntes.

candidateObjective: 新人に釘打ち位置を示し、間違いを直すよう支援的な言葉で伝える。
candidateFocus: ～てください gives a clear instruction, ～ないでください prohibits overdriving, and ～たら orders a correction after checking the nail head.

archivedSpeaking.opening: この線が釘打ち範囲です。ここに打ってください。釘の頭が沈んだら空気圧を調整しましょう。大丈夫です。一緒に確認します。
archivedSpeaking.goal: Coach a new crew member on nail placement and depth. Show the nailing zone, correct high and overdriven nails with clear Japanese requests, and keep a supportive tone.

reader.sourceSpanish: Hoy Kevin usa la pistola de clavos por primera vez, y Rogelio se queda a su lado.
reader.sourceEnglish: Today Kevin uses the nail gun for the first time, and Rogelio stays at his side.
reader.candidateJapanese: 今日、ケビンは初めて釘打ち機を使い、ロヘリオがそばで見守ります。
reader.archivedJapanese: 今日、ケビンは初めて釘打ち機を使い、ロヘリオがそばで見守ります。
reader.archivedEnglish: Today Kevin uses the nail gun for the first time, and Rogelio stays at his side.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Antes de empezar, revisa la manguera y el compresor, y no pongas el dedo en el gatillo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Before you start, check the hose and the compressor, and don't put your finger on the trigger.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「始める前にホースとコンプレッサーを確認し、引き金に指を掛けないでください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Before you start, check the hose and the compressor, and don't put your finger on the trigger.
reader.reviewNote: Nail-gun handling instruction requires qualified tool/safety review.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Mira esta línea en la teja; esta es la zona de clavado.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Look at this line on the shingle; this is the nailing zone.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「シングル材のこの線を見てください。ここが釘打ち範囲です。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「シングル材のこの線を見てください。ここが釘打ち範囲です。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Look at this line on the shingle; this is the nailing zone.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Clávalo aquí, en la zona de clavado, y sigue el patrón de clavado del fabricante.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Nail it here, in the nailing zone, and follow the manufacturer's nail pattern.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「釘打ち範囲の中のここに打ち、メーカーの釘打ちパターンに従ってください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Nail it here, in the nailing zone, and follow the manufacturer's nail pattern.
reader.reviewNote: Nailing zone and pattern are manufacturer-specific.

reader.sourceSpanish: Kevin clava la primera teja, pero un clavo queda muy alto.
reader.sourceEnglish: Kevin nails the first shingle, but one nail ends up too high.
reader.candidateJapanese: ケビンは最初のシングル材に釘を打ちますが、一本は高すぎる位置に入ります。
reader.archivedJapanese: ケビンは最初のシングル材に釘を打ちますが、一本は高すぎる位置に入ります。
reader.archivedEnglish: Kevin nails the first shingle, but one nail ends up too high.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Ese clavo muy alto no agarra bien la teja de abajo; sácalo y ponle otro.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: That high nail doesn't hold the shingle below well; pull it out and put in another one.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「その高すぎる位置の釘では、下のシングル材を十分に留められません。抜いて別の釘を打ってください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: That high nail doesn't hold the shingle below well; pull it out and put in another one.
reader.reviewNote: High-nail removal and replacement are product-specific.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Y el agujero, séllalo según las instrucciones del producto; no lo dejes abierto.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: And the hole, seal it according to the product instructions; don't leave it open.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「穴は製品の説明書に従ってシーリングしてください。開いたままにしないでください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: And the hole, seal it according to the product instructions; don't leave it open.
reader.reviewNote: Hole sealing method must follow the actual selected product instructions.

reader.sourceSpanish: Luego Kevin dispara otro clavo, y la cabeza del clavo se hunde en la teja.
reader.sourceEnglish: Then Kevin fires another nail, and the nail head sinks into the shingle.
reader.candidateJapanese: 次にケビンが別の釘を打つと、釘の頭がシングル材に沈み込みます。
reader.archivedJapanese: 次にケビンが別の釘を打つと、釘の頭がシングル材に沈み込みます。
reader.archivedEnglish: Then Kevin fires another nail, and the nail head sinks into the shingle.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Fíjate bien en la cabeza del clavo; tiene que quedar al ras, no más abajo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Look closely at the nail head; it has to sit flush, not lower.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「釘の頭をよく見てください。表面と面一で、低くなってはいけません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Look closely at the nail head; it has to sit flush, not lower.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Un clavo demasiado hundido corta la teja, y el viento la puede levantar.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: An overdriven nail cuts the shingle, and the wind can lift it.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「深く打ち込みすぎた釘はシングル材を切り、風で持ち上がることがあります。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: An overdriven nail cuts the shingle, and the wind can lift it.
reader.reviewNote: Wind uplift consequence is plausible but product/installation context matters.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Bájale a la presión de aire un poco y prueba otra vez; no lo hundas.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Turn the air pressure down a little and try again; don't sink it.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「空気圧を少し下げて、もう一度試してください。深く打ち込みすぎないでください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Turn the air pressure down a little and try again; don't sink it.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Si la profundidad cambia, avísame y lo ajustamos juntos.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: If the depth changes, let me know and we'll adjust it together.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「深さが変わったら教えてください。一緒に調整しましょう。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「深さが変わったら教えてください。一緒に調整しましょう。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: If the depth changes, let me know and we'll adjust it together.

reader.sourceSpanish: Kevin se pone rojo, pero Rogelio le dice: No te preocupes, a todos nos pasó.
reader.sourceEnglish: Kevin turns red, but Rogelio tells him: Don't worry, it happened to all of us.
reader.candidateJapanese: ケビンは顔を赤らめますが、ロヘリオは「大丈夫です。誰にでも起こることです」と伝えます。
reader.archivedJapanese: ケビンは顔を赤らめますが、ロヘリオは「大丈夫です。誰にでも起こることです」と伝えます。
reader.archivedEnglish: Kevin turns red, but Rogelio tells him: Don't worry, it happened to all of us.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Y la pistola, no la apuntes hacia nadie, ni en broma.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: And the gun, don't point it at anyone, not even as a joke.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「釘打ち機を人に向けないでください。冗談でもいけません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: And the gun, don't point it at anyone, not even as a joke.
reader.reviewNote: Gun direction is safety-critical; preserve meaning and qualified review.

reader.sourceSpanish: Más tarde llega don Ernesto, un trabajador nuevo con muchos años de experiencia en otra compañía.
reader.sourceEnglish: Later Don Ernesto arrives, a new worker with many years of experience at another company.
reader.candidateJapanese: その後、別の会社で長年働いた新人のエルネストさんが来ます。
reader.archivedJapanese: その後、別の会社で長年働いた新人のエルネストさんが来ます。
reader.archivedEnglish: Later Don Ernesto arrives, a new worker with many years of experience at another company.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Don Ernesto, aquí clavamos así; revíselo usted también, por favor.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Don Ernesto, here we nail like this; please check it yourself too.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「エルネストさん、ここではこのように釘を打ちます。ご自身でも確認してください。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「エルネストさん、ここではこのように釘を打ちます。ご自身でも確認してください。」

say.label: Coach a new roofer on nail placement with clear, supportive instructions.

write.label: Write a correction for a high nail and a separate correction for an overdriven nail.

curriculumAdaptationNote: The scene teaches supportive correction of nail placement. Preserve the source distinction between high and overdriven nails, the product-specific nailing zone/pattern, hole sealing according to product instructions, and nail-gun handling. Do not turn the fictional tool adjustments into universal scored instructions. Archived Japanese is evidence only; grammar and five Spanish verbs are pinned separately. No selected learner/audio text or progress identity is created.
